newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes climb with stock-driven WTIs.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes climb with stock-driven WTIs.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes climbed with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude early Friday, following reports of tighter U.S. inventories.
Prices for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude tracked a 15-cent rise in WTI, while differentials were flat in a market that saw litte business this week because of holidays.
U.S. supplies of crude oil fell 5.1 million barrels last week, according to the key industry group American Petroleum Institute.
The ANS diff was $1.70 off Feb. WTI, though a key producer said he would accept bids for Jan. delivery off Februay WTI.

His official offer stood at $1.60 off February WTI.
Flat diffs and higher WTI prices lifted ANS 15 cents from Thursday to $23.45/23.65 a barrel.
Kern River prices stayed at $18.65/18.75 a barrel after companies lifted postings late last week.
Discounts remained 10 cents below to even with postings, traders said.
Wilmington crude, produced offshore in Long Beach, Calif., also was flat at $20.15/20.25 a barrel.
